title: Negotiate PHXP asynchronously without weakening ownership
description:
## Parent

`phx-1ir`

## What to build

Integrate PHXP into the Tokio path using bounded blocking capacity where needed while preserving authentication, framing, descriptor validation, and irreversible ownership semantics.

Authoritative design: `docs/public-hosting-hardening-design.md` and `docs/public-hosting-hardening-implementation-plan.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At most 256 PHXP operations and 32 probe workers contribute to validated `TasksMax` demand without unbounded queued work.
- [ ] Cancellation before descriptor delivery may relay; cancellation/failure after delivery never relays.
- [ ] Existing Linux and macOS receivers and handoff regression suites remain compatible.

## Blocked by

- `phx-1f6` — Serve bounded ClientHello routing on Tokio
- `phx-1iq` — Activate late Workloads with production PHXP endpoints
close_reason: Resolved in eec193d6463e0965e2c005055533d3c27f190eb9 with Darwin cfg correction efe3eccc0a6ee5cee927ae39099dc3a1f8ced7b6; revalidated at exact commit 8a9b4dc5064e9e23406e0e0773e18d8a86a57959 after blocker phx-3a3 closed. PHXP now acquires one of at most 256 permits before tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so no attacker-controlled blocking queue forms; TasksMax demand also counts all 256 PHXP operations and 32 probe workers. Only handoff::Outcome::Unavailable retains a TcpStream eligible for relay; Transferred and Delivered are irreversible and never relay. Regression: proxy::tests::saturated_async_handoff_falls_back_without_queueing. Capacity regression: ingress_limits::tests::task_budget_counts_every_bounded_handoff_and_probe_worker. Linux gates: cargo fmt -- --check; cargo test; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --manifest-path samples/rust/Cargo.toml; cargo test --manifest-path integrations/elixir/phx_port_handoff/native/phx_port_handoff_native/Cargo.toml. macOS root DoD: PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo fmt -- --check; PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo test; PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings. Literal macOS CI receiver gates: PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo build --verbose; PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo test --verbose; PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo test --manifest-path samples/rust/Cargo.toml --verbose; PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo test --manifest-path integrations/elixir/phx_port_handoff/native/phx_port_handoff_native/Cargo.toml --verbose. macOS Elixir integration gate: cd integrations/elixir/phx_port_handoff && PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:$PATH mix test. Results: root 122 unit tests plus all integration targets passed; Rust sample 27 passed; native broker 9 passed; ExUnit 12 passed. macOS checkout restored clean to master at fc0d7af9007d08ad19a7802afecf192886edf612 and all temporary phx-115 refs removed.

comments.text: Blocked after candidate commits eec193d and efe3ecc. Linux Definition of Done passed: cargo fmt -- --check; cargo test; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings. The clean macOS checkout was fast-forwarded to efe3eccc0a6ee5cee927ae39099dc3a1f8ced7b6. Darwin cargo fmt and all PHXP/root tests passed, including descriptor transfer, partial-send ownership, and inert-descriptor acknowledgement behavior, but the required full command failed before clippy in ingress_config::tests::public_observability_is_loopback_only_bounded_and_explicitly_expiring. That pre-existing test captures SystemTime::now(), writes expires_at_unix_seconds = now + 3601, then production loading reads the wall clock again; if at least one second elapses, the remaining duration is accepted as <= 3600. title: Publish bounded metrics and privacy-preserving events
description:
## Parent

`phx-z3w`

## What to build

Expose optional loopback-only Prometheus output and structured stderr events that make route, capacity, handoff, relay, and reload state operable without attacker-driven cardinality.

Authoritative design: `docs/public-hosting-hardening-design.md` and `docs/public-hosting-hardening-implementation-plan.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Metric labels are limited to bounded declared identities and never include source IP, arbitrary SNI, connection IDs, certificates, or error strings.
- [ ] Prometheus response size and listener exposure are bounded and provide no mutation path.
- [ ] Sampled source diagnostics require explicit expiry and normal logs omit source IP.

## Blocked by

- `phx-27w` — Authorize machine-readable health and root-only mutation
- `phx-2x5` — Expose bounded overload events without log amplification
close_reason: Resolved in e3933193e728aa10efc05a590e910e682f66f345. Added a GET-only loopback Prometheus listener with 1 MiB responses, fixed-enum and bounded Route Declaration metrics, rate-limited structured route/delivery/reload events, and explicitly expiring sampled source diagnostics while preserving default development activation. Regression: tests/observability.rs::metrics_listener_is_bounded_read_only_and_uses_only_declared_labels, source_diagnostics_are_sampled_only_before_the_explicit_expiry, and unavailable_metrics_listener_does_not_stop_the_data_plane.

title: Drain async ingress with explicit ownership-aware cancellation
description:
## Parent

`phx-1ir`

## What to build

Coordinate activated listeners, pre-routing tasks, PHXP negotiations, relays, state flush, and endpoint cleanup through the accepted shutdown state machine.

Authoritative design: `docs/public-hosting-hardening-design.md` and `docs/public-hosting-hardening-implementation-plan.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admission stops immediately and pre-routing cancels without leaks.
- [ ] PHXP ownership resolves safely; handed-off connections survive ingress exit.
- [ ] Relays drain for at most 60 seconds, then close with a bounded diagnostic and controlled shutdown.

## Blocked by

- `phx-ok1` — Relay TLS asynchronously with half-close and idle policy
- `phx-115` — Negotiate PHXP asynchronously without weakening ownership
close_reason: Resolved in 8a362c6d9a975ab6f4d3960a948dbc63fe738ffb. Admission and pre-routing now stop by direct shutdown notification; PHXP ownership resolves before bounded runtime exit; established relays drain to one shared deadline; pending relay establishment is cancellation-aware and RelayStarted is linearized against shutdown; active control and metrics requests use absolute deadlines and final-exit cancellation. Regressions: shutdown_drains_established_relay_until_shared_deadline, shutdown_cancels_pre_routing_without_leaking_admission, shutdown_waits_for_phxp_ownership_and_handoff_survives, shutdown_cancels_pending_relay_establishment_before_start, relay_start_commit_is_atomic_with_shutdown_request, shutdown_wakes_idle_listener_without_timer_progress, partial_local_requests_cannot_outlive_daemon_shutdown, clean_shutdown_emits_one_bounded_drain_event. Linux commands: cargo fmt -- --check; cargo test; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings. macOS checkout ~/phx-port at exact commit 8a362c6d9a975ab6f4d3960a948dbc63fe738ffb: PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo fmt -- --check && PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo test && PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Resolution and source commit

Resolved CP-06 in source commit 27d2d9805bc907960f8fd7dda6003fe568f02f84. Confirmed against baseline 8b51d81f92a46b963ba48ed77ee73a7b91aa116f: HOME-prefix removal and absolute-root removal produced identical tree segments for distinct Port Registry keys. The display tree now retains complete Path components, including filesystem roots, and uses native path joining when collapsing chains. Platform: Linux x86_64. rustc 1.95.0-nightly (f134bbc78 2026-01-24); cargo 1.95.0-nightly (efcd9f586 2026-01-23). Current manifests and lockfiles were used without dependency changes or restoration.

- After the source fix, the identical watchdog-bounded command exited 0: all five tests passed, no tests ignored, test execution 0.01s. Both ordinary URL tree and --port-only modes cover HOME/project versus /project, external and HOME-string-prefix sibling paths, logical IDs versus absolute project paths, existing HOME grouping, and named roles. - `cargo check --locked` exited 0.

All three CP-06 acceptance criteria are satisfied by the CLI tests: colliding names keep both assignments in both tree modes; external and prefix-sibling paths remain correctly absolute; logical identities remain distinct, flat output preserves original keys, and every invocation leaves the fixture registry byte-identical. Fixtures use private temporary HOME directories and explicit registry overrides; external absolute paths are data-only keys and are never created or opened. Temporary directories are automatically removed and all short-lived CLI children are reaped.

No Darwin execution is claimed or required for CP-06. The separately tracked CP-05 root-node-with-children rendering issue remains out of scope for its dependent follow-up. comments.author: Christian Geuer-Pollmann
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Remediation evidence - ING-R3

Source commit: 58592cec6e0e4fffe7aa2462ad950f84bbf1588e (fix: bound control connection and request deadlines (phx-14e)). Baseline: 0a08308. Copilot session: 36e03679-5457-45d2-b0fa-9066c7401b33. Selected this initially-ready P2 issue in audit-rust-elixir-2026-09-astra after confirming E5/phx-324 was already closed; no peer issue was claimed or changed.

### Confirmed finding and fix

The finding is confirmed by executed, isolated Linux CLI regressions, not only source inspection. Both query_control and duplicate-daemon startup blocked in UnixStream::connect before any I/O timeout applied. Per-read timeouts allowed a trickled response to run past the overall budget; connection and response waits also accumulated. A stream/seqpacket protocol mismatch reproduced an operational connect error that caused startup to unlink and replace the existing endpoint (different inode).

Extracted the existing nonblocking PHXP connector into src/unix_socket.rs with typed io::Error results and reused it for control connections. Control clients now carry one checked two-second absolute deadline across connection, request writes, half-close, and all response reads. ### Confirmed cause and fix

The actual Darwin sender renewed per-operation socket timeouts while assembling valid fragmented READY and ADOPTED frames. The awaited blocking worker also did not observe caller cancellation before descriptor delivery. One absolute one-second deadline now starts before connect and covers HELLO, READY, the initial descriptor-bearing send, remaining HANDOFF bytes, and acknowledgement. Nonblocking control I/O recomputes the remaining budget and polls at most 25 ms between cancellation checks.

The shared ING-R3 Unix connector is unchanged. Its caller now supplies the same exchange deadline rather than allocating a fresh connect budget. Dropping the awaiting ingress task closes a oneshot receiver; the Darwin worker observes that signal only before delivery. Connect itself remains governed by the existing bounded connector, with cancellation checked before and after it, not a new connector implementation or retry loop.

Positive sendmsg results return unchanged before any subsequent timeout/cancellation check. `finish_delivery` consumes the client socket, disables caller cancellation, and can return only Transferred or Delivered. Even a deadline reached immediately after SCM_RIGHTS delivery cannot return Unavailable. The sender retains its inert descriptor until the bounded post-delivery outcome and never calls shutdown on it.

Pre-fix committed regression: `0e88357763fc2f70e69589412cf1a4f877d4929b`, retained at `refs/campaign/phx-2ww-303355da/regression-v3` locally and on the authorized Mac. - Valid READY and ADOPTED, each one byte every 20 ms: 1.575121500 s, complete ADOPTED accepted instead of expiring the shared budget.
- Aborted awaiting task before READY: blocking handoff/global/pre-routing admission remained occupied for 1.006262416 s instead of promptly observing cancellation.

An earlier two-test Darwin reproduction also failed (READY 1.854932375 s, combined exchange 2.204676542 s). Running the existing formatter on the installer produced no installer source diff or semantic change. CONTEXT.md, accepted ADRs, runtime code, manifests, and lockfiles are unchanged.

## Failing and passing regression

The new test copies the actual package formatter configuration into an ExUnit-owned mode-0700 fixture directory and writes intentionally unformatted Elixir at priv/installer/igniter.exs. It requires the normal Mix check to reject that path, then runs normal Mix formatting and requires a clean recheck plus the exact formatted fixture text. It does not use an explicit filename argument to bypass the input selection under test. Child Mix VMs use two schedulers, exit synchronously, and the fixture is removed by on_exit.

All Mix commands below ran from phx_port_handoff on Linux x86_64, Elixir/Mix 1.20.4, Erlang/OTP 29, ERTS 17.0.6 (Elixir compiled with OTP 28).

Before the fix:
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix test test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs -> exit 2, 1/2 passed. The existing installation/idempotence test passed; the new regression failed because the formatter incorrectly returned exit 0 for the unformatted installer.
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix test test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs:65 --seed 0 -> exit 2, the same deterministic regression failure.

After the fix:
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix test test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs -> exit 0, 2 passed in 1.6 seconds, including unchanged installation/idempotence behavior.

## Definition of Done evidence

These final commands all exited 0:
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix format .formatter.exs priv/installer/igniter.exs test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix format --check-formatted .formatter.exs priv/installer/igniter.exs test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix format --check-formatted
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- timeout --kill-after=10s 180s mix test test/phx_port_handoff_install_test.exs
- From the repository root: git diff --check, git diff --cached --check, and git diff --exit-code -- phx_port_handoff/priv/installer/igniter.exs.

No separate Elixir linter is configured for this component; existing formatter and compiler warning gates were used without adding tools. The complete diff was reviewed and only the three explicit owned source/documentation paths were staged in the source commit.

One intermediate attempt placed priv/installer inside a brace glob and failed with filelib badpattern/missing_delimiter. That attempt was corrected to the explicit file input before the successful complete validation above; it is not counted as a passing run.

## Acceptance, limitations, and cleanup

All three acceptance criteria are satisfied: default formatting covers the shipped installer, existing formatter output is clean with no installer behavior change, and the intentionally unformatted isolated fixture proves red-before/green-after behavior. No dependencies were installed or changed. No PHXP sender harness, production service, real private key, canary, or Mac checkout was touched; all trust/resource invariants are unchanged. Darwin execution is not required for this tooling-only issue and none is claimed.

Access to the external /home/chgeuer/github/pnezis/probex/probex executable was denied. command -v probex was recorded, but no alternate executable was invoked; repository files were read using the prompt-authorized fallback. No source-file denial occurred. All owned fixture processes exited, fixture cleanup completed, and no cleanup remains outstanding.

The current-code finding was confirmed against `ece64c0` with a regression added before the fix. The regression exercises actual public reconciliation, exact-hostname TLS verification against a generated fixture certificate on an ephemeral loopback listener, and the real private-state load/atomic-publication seam at all 1,000 supported declarations. Test-only thread-local counters record actual derived-state reads, successful publications, and aggregate route entries written.

| Phase | Before reads / writes / entries written | After reads / writes / entries written |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cold cache | 1000 / 1000 / 500500 | 1 / 1 / 1000 |
| Unchanged restart, empty active table | 1000 / 1000 / 1000000 | 1 / 0 / 0 |
| Bulk certificate rotation | 1000 / 1000 / 1000000 | 1 / 1 / 1000 |
| Unchanged warm TLS refresh | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Reconciliation now collects at most one proof per bounded declaration set entry and performs one compare/update transaction per pass. Single-route activation shares the same prepare/persist/publish path. Generation, exact declaration target, stale observation, expiry, and capacity checks remain before publication, with observation and expiry rechecked before activation. Reload pruning uses the same transaction; routing/profile locks are released before disk I/O. Private byte limits and atomic replacement remain enforced. Conditional publication still persists genuine legacy Port Registry migration. No new dependency, database, unbounded queue, TLS bypass, or descriptor-ownership change was introduced.

## Executed regression and Definition of Done

Platform: Linux x86_64. `rustc 1.95.0-nightly (f134bbc78 2026-01-24)`; `cargo 1.95.0-nightly (efcd9f586 2026-01-23)`. All commands ran at the repository root with the current lockfile.

Before fix, the following command exited 101 on exactly the operation-count assertion above, after all four phases completed (145.32 seconds):

```text
timeout --kill-after=10s 240s cargo test --locked --bin phx-port proxy::tests::reconciled_cache_publication_is_coalesced_at_route_scale -- --exact
```

After fix, the following command passed all four operation-count phases (1 passed, exit 0):

```text
timeout --kill-after=10s 180s cargo test --locked --bin phx-port proxy::tests::reconciled_cache_publication_is_coalesced_at_route_scale -- --exact --nocapture
```

The final combined targeted gate passed 40 tests, 0 failed, 0 ignored (25.00 seconds, exit 0):

```text
timeout --kill-after=10s 240s cargo test --locked --bin phx-port -- proxy::tests::reconciled_cache_ proxy::tests::cache_persistence_ proxy::tests::unchanged_certificate_ proxy::tests::reload_ proxy::tests::stale_reconciliation_ proxy::tests::bounded_reconciliation_ proxy::tests::cancelled_reconciliation_ proxy::tests::reconciliation_probes_ proxy::tests::foreground_probes_ proxy::tests::late_public_workload_ proxy::tests::declared_certificate_rotation_ proxy::tests::multiple_declared_routes_ proxy::tests::public_route_ proxy::tests::verified_routes_ proxy::tests::removed_registration_ proxy::tests::three_tcp_failures_ proxy::tests::development_ route_cache::tests:: port_registry::tests:: --test-threads=1
```

Compilation, both lint commands, formatting, and whitespace review all passed. The targeted tests include concurrent reload/prune ordering, unlocked warm routing/status during persistence, unchanged warm refresh, stale/expired/mixed-validity batches, rejected old generations, byte-limit rejection without active or disk changes, bounded batch input and eviction, deadline progress, exact certificate/Workload routing, and development migration. One intermediate new cache-test fixture failed because its temporary directory was 0755; the fixture was corrected to the existing required 0700. The final gate passed without relaxing that policy or suppressing diagnostics.

## Limits and cleanup

The 1,000-route operation-count test uses a 60-second per-pass test budget to collect all proofs in one pass. It is not a claim that 1,000 certificates finish verification in the production one-second pass, nor a wall-clock production performance claim. A separate 300ms integration gate proves completed proofs are published when later Workload probes stall. The production pass deadline and bounded probe workers remain intact, with a bounded slice reserved for publication.

Evidence is Linux execution plus source review; this issue requires no Darwin gate. No Mac checkout, service, canary, production socket, or real private key was accessed or changed. No freezing BEAM harness was run. Fixture threads/listeners were joined/closed and temporary directories were removed by test cleanup; no owned fixture process remains.
